methodology_note: The grading-model facts in review.md and the verified-scorer description check out against the snapshot and the working-repo _verified_db_match. The reviews reconstruct solutions from primary sources, recompute reward tables, and replay alternatives, and every load-bearing number I re-derived for 17 tasks matched (the floor/half-up sets for 017-022 and 026, task_023's anniversary windows, task_016's referral rows, task_010's referral-link failure). Two blind spots. First, task_015 tested an alternative DB state (an extra verification_history row) that the conversation cannot produce, because the customer holds only one identity field; alternative-path replays should be checked for reachability against the scenario before they count as a defect. Second, task_014 took 'the more specific document wins' as settling a contradiction, which conflicts with the calibration's two-readings rule. Under the verified scorer none of the 20 assigned verdicts depends on the relaxed comparisons: none involves closure_reason or extra discoverable reads, and the failure modes found (user_discoverable_tools, user_discoverable_tool_calls, cash_back_disputes, credit_card_transaction_history, credit_card_applications) are in exactly-compared tables, so these verdicts should match an upstream-scorer run.
